ads.title: Every Experience Matters
ads.primary_text:
If you were handed one do-over, what would you use it on?

Yianni Bourbakis was asked exactly that and answered in one word. Nothing.

He would not trade any of it. The person he is came out of the things he went through.

Co-Owner, Elia Mediterranean Grille.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer

ads.title: A Home With Soul
ads.primary_text:
Why do so many beautiful houses feel like nobody lives in them?

Betsy Wentz calls it a soulless home, and she refuses to build one.

She makes clients sit in her studio and pull fabrics until she can see what makes them tick. The house has to come out of them.

Founder, Betsy Wentz Interior Design.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer

ads.title: What My Son Taught Me
ads.primary_text:
What has your child taught you that you could not have learned anywhere else?

Jason Esch calls his oldest son a superhuman being and says he learns from him every day.

Patience. Presence. Enjoying the small things. His other children are better people for growing up alongside him.

President and Owner, TeamLogic IT Pittsburgh.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer
ads.guest_title: President and Owner, TeamLogic IT Pittsburgh

ads.title: Leadership Gaps in the Next Generation
ads.primary_text:
What makes someone worth following?

Jason Esch believes the next generation will lead through the relationships they choose to invest in.

He also names the hard part. The inspiring side of leadership does not work unless you are willing to be vulnerable and relatable.

President and Owner, TeamLogic IT Pittsburgh.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer
ads.guest_title: President and Owner, TeamLogic IT Pittsburgh

ads.title: A Career of Continuous Learning
ads.primary_text:
When did you last take a pay cut and feel lucky about it?

Ezra Shapiro left an office job for twelve dollars an hour in a kitchen.

He went home every night thinking about what he had cooked and what he would cook tomorrow. He figured he could spend a lifetime in kitchens and still not be finished learning.

Private chef.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer

ads.title: Creating Meaningful Change
ads.primary_text:
What part of your work would you keep if you had to give up the rest?

Beth Vietmeier runs the marketing and the events and genuinely loves both.

The part she would keep is the nonprofit work. Changing one person's life is the thing she believes she is here to do.

Founder, Valiant 3 Communications.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer

ads.title: What Truly Fills Her Cup
ads.primary_text:
What does someone who raises money for a children's hospital love most about the job?

Rachel Petrucelli said the donors, and it surprised the person asking her.

She sits with people deciding what their own hard-earned money should do in the world, and helps them find the answer. She calls that a privilege.

President, UPMC Children's Hospital Foundation.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer

ads.title: Falling in Love With the Process
ads.primary_text:
What happens the first time you genuinely put in the work?

Chris Lee had never done it before law school. Class every day, studying until nine, every Sunday gone.

He fell in love with the process itself, the way he had watched great coaches do. The results came after that, and the confidence came with them.

Managing Director and COO, Dickie McCamey.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer
ads.guest_title: Managing Director and COO, Dickie McCamey

ads.title: Learning Through Reading
ads.primary_text:
What is the advice for getting good at anything?

Ezra Shapiro says it in two words. Just read.

Before anyone paid him to cook, he worked through chef biographies, cookbooks and books on the business of running a restaurant, and practiced in his spare time.

Private chef.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer

ads.title: Proactive, Not Reactive
ads.primary_text:
How much can your doctor learn about you in seven minutes?

That is the appointment most of us get. Cut the carbs, see you in a year.

Dr. Sunjay Mannan sits at his patients' kitchen tables for two hours instead, working out what is actually going on before it becomes an emergency.

Founder, Health Is Wealth Concierge Medicine.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer
ads.guest_title: Founder, Health Is Wealth Concierge Medicine

ads.title: How He Handles Stress
ads.primary_text:
Does your doctor follow his own advice?

Dr. Sunjay Mannan handles his stress the way he tells his patients to handle theirs.

Sleep protected. Workouts in. Nothing on the plate he knows will affect his head. The stress is coming either way, so he prepares for it.

Founder, Health Is Wealth Concierge Medicine.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer
ads.guest_title: Founder, Health Is Wealth Concierge Medicine

ads.title: Modeling Self-Care
ads.primary_text:
What is your child learning from the way you work?

Dr. Sunjay Mannan puts his daughter on the bus in the morning and makes the Boy Scout meeting at night.

He has brought her along on patient visits so she can watch him spend an hour on a blood pressure check. What he wants her to take from it is that she gets to build her life on her own terms.

Founder, Health Is Wealth Concierge Medicine.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer
ads.guest_title: Founder, Health Is Wealth Concierge Medicine

ads.title: Not Just Dinner
ads.primary_text:
What makes a dinner the one people still talk about a year later?

Ezra Shapiro cooks in other people's homes, for four guests or for twenty.

The menu gets built around one person at the table. If it is your husband's fiftieth, the whole night is designed to land on him.

Private chef.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer

ads.title: The Mindset
ads.primary_text:
What do you call it when you can see something that is not there yet?

Yianni Bourbakis calls it vision.

The restaurant is named Elia, the Greek word for olive, after the tree his country gathers under. He tells his chefs the main ingredient in any recipe is love.

Co-Owner, Elia Mediterranean Grille.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer

ads.title: They Sold a Ring to Start
ads.primary_text:
What would you sell to bet on yourselves?

Lou and Veronica Guarino sold her wedding ring for ten thousand dollars.

A client had been asking to buy that ring for years. They took him up on it, and that money started the store.

Co-Owners, Louis Anthony Jewelers.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer

ads.title: Make People Feel at Home
ads.primary_text:
What can a jeweler learn from watching a hospital president pick up litter?

Walking through Children's Hospital, the Guarinos saw its president reach down for a piece of paper on the floor.

Her rule for her staff was that the hospital is your home, and you would not leave paper on the floor at home. Everything matters, down to who is at the front door.

Co-Owners, Louis Anthony Jewelers.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer

ads.title: First to the NHL
ads.primary_text:
Did you ever really believe in the thing you were working toward?

Ryan Malone grew up in St. Clair watching his father play for the Penguins, and became the first Pittsburgh-raised player to reach the NHL.

He is honest that he never thought it was actually attainable. It sat in the back of his mind as motivation through the early mornings.

Retired NHL player, Malone Family Foundation.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer
ads.guest_title: Retired NHL player, Malone Family Foundation

ads.title: A Harder Chapter
ads.primary_text:
What was the bravest thing Ryan Malone ever did?

It happened nowhere near a rink. He checked himself into a hospital and asked for help.

Greg calls that hero stuff and says it counts for more than anything he did in the NHL. Plenty of the people who need that help never make the call.

Retired NHL player, Malone Family Foundation.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer
ads.guest_title: Retired NHL player, Malone Family Foundation

ads.title: It Takes a Team
ads.primary_text:
What has to happen before a business can grow past one person?

Bill Sarris says you learn to hand the work to other people.

You cannot do it all yourself. He calls it the hardest question anyone can ask a founder.

Owner, Sarris Candies.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer

ads.title: The Margin of Excellence
ads.primary_text:
What does a donation to a children's hospital actually pay for?

Rachel Petrucelli calls it the margin of excellence.

Giving is what puts a rheumatologist, a heart doctor and a geneticist in the same city as the family who needs them, so a sick child does not have to travel for care.

President, UPMC Children's Hospital Foundation.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer

ads.title: Treat People the Right Way
ads.primary_text:
How does a law firm treat the lawyers on the other side of the case?

At Chris Lee's firm, the same way it treats its own people.

Employees, partners, opposing counsel, all of it. They go to court prepared and they protect their clients hard, and they do it professionally.

Managing Director and COO, Dickie McCamey.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer
ads.guest_title: Managing Director and COO, Dickie McCamey

ads.title: The Case That Defined a Career
ads.primary_text:
What does it do to a lawyer to catch a case that size?

In 2003 a hepatitis A outbreak at a restaurant in the Beaver Valley Mall affected a thousand people, the largest in the country at that point.

Chris Lee got the case. The FDA, the CDC and the national news arrived at once, and some of the people involved died. It shaped how he has practiced ever since.

Managing Director and COO, Dickie McCamey.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer
ads.guest_title: Managing Director and COO, Dickie McCamey

ads.title: Why I Built Mileage
ads.primary_text:
Should you master one thing, or try everything first?

Bill Bishilany built his company on trying everything.

Human-centered design taught him that the wider the range of experience on a team, the better equipped it is to solve a hard problem. He thinks the younger generation needs to hear that.

Founder, Mileage Design.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer

ads.title: The Other Side of Hard
ads.primary_text:
Is everything you want really on the other side of hard?

Bill Bishilany had that line framed in his office, and then he rewrote it.

His version says everything you have ever wanted is on the other side of happiness. Be happy first, and the rest follows.

Founder, Mileage Design.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
ads.headline: Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer

ads.title: The Mosaic
ads.primary_text:
Why does good marketing still fail?

Bill Bishilany describes the work as a mosaic where every tile has to be there.

Design and build. Site structure. Targeting the words your future clients actually search. Miss one tile and the picture never quite comes together.

Founder, Mileage Design.

Living Your Legacy with Greg Weimer. New episodes on YouTube.
